messages:
sam: Heads-up: spun up a 1% canary for v4-quant-lite on the multi-turn and long-doc routes. We used the new route-split by doc-length hash (<=2k tokens -> short, >2k -> long). Initial telemetry looks ok for short, but long-doc slice showing instability in answer coherence.

jen: quick ask  are we running the new paired-permutation analysis or the old bootstrap? need consistent comparison across runs.

sam: paired permutation for primary metric (answer-coherence @ top1), bootstrap for auxiliary (halluc-rate). Both ran on a 30m window.

omar: numbers?

sam: short-doc: coherence +0.4% (CI crosses 0). long-doc: coherence -2.7% (p<0.01 paired-perm), hallucination +1.6pp (keyword detector), p95 latency +60ms (small). sample sizes long-doc control=4.8k, variant=1.2k (low).

cheng: variant sample looks small  did we route by session or request? small sample could bias long-doc because sessions with long docs are rarer and sticky.

sam: routed by session hash but we didn't enforce session stickiness across upgrades; some variant sessions are short-lived.

jen: for this kind of slice we should require min_effective_samples=2000 and min_sessions=800 before evaluating. Also, ramp step for long-doc should be 0.25/0.75/1.5% not 1/2/5.

ops-bot: canary event: v4-quant-lite -> 1% (sam)

eva: two operational notes: 1) kernel k9-quant has a microcode tweak that reduces beam-scorer stability on long contexts; 2) the quant fallback pool (v4fp16) is available as a drop-in for >2k token docs. Could we route long-docs to fp16 automatically if we detect coherence drop?

omar: auto-route-to-fp16 on degradation is exactly a per-slice fallback we need. but be careful: switching runtime mid-session can lose KV cache compatibility. need session-aware fallback (only for new sessions) or a graceful degrade path.

sam: agree. propose policy: per-slice fallback trigger = coherence_drop >= 1.5% AND halluc_inc >= 1.0pp over a rolling 20m window with min_samples=2000 -> route new sessions in that slice to v4fp16; keep old sessions pinned to original variant until end-of-session.

cheng: also we should capture a sample of 250 failing pairs (control+variant) in the console for immediate triage, include raw context, model logits, and kernel rev.

jen: adding: before any ramp beyond 1% for long-doc, run a preflight smokecheck: sample 500 long-doc queries from corpus A (diverse length/genre) and assert coherence >= baseline - 1.0% and halluc <= baseline + 0.8pp. if fail, block ramp.

sam: I'll update the canary config now. snippet (sanitized):

```json
{"canary": {"initial": "0.01", "ramps": ["0.01","0.02","0.05"], "slices": {"long-doc": {"token_thresh": 2000, "min_effective_samples": 2000, "fallback_policy": "route_new_sessions_to_v4fp16", "coherence_drop_pct_threshold": 1.5, "halluc_pp_threshold": 1.0}}, "preflight": {"long-doc": {"smokecheck_samples": 500, "coherence_margin_pct": 1.0, "halluc_margin_pp": 0.8}}}}
```

omar: good. two implementation notes: 1) gatebook needs a new action type: route_new_sessions_to_variant with session-pin semantics; 2) console should display a compact failing-pair carousel for the slice.

ops-bot: alert: long-doc slice coherence delta exceeded configured threshold (rolling 20m)

eva: ops-bot posted links to sampled pairs in bucket s3://redwood-experiments/1830004444/failed_pairs.tar.gz

cheng: given the small variant n (1.2k) we probably hit a transient bias. i'd like to hold rollback until min_samples=2000 reached, but auto-fallback could be enabled to route new sessions to fp16 immediately to limit user impact.

sam: implemented that: live config change to enable fallback routing for new sessions only. keeping variant at 0.5% short-doc, 0.25% long-doc now. will re-run paired-permutation with updated session stickiness.

jen: follow-ups: 1) add kernel-rev to rollout metadata and expose in console; 2) add preflight smokecheck enforcement to gatebook; 3) document session-aware fallback semantics in runbook. who takes these?

eva: I'll own kernel-rev in metadata and upload a compatibility matrix linking kernel rev -> observed long-doc regressions.

omar: i'll own the gatebook change and the session-routing action.

cheng: i'll add the smokecheck enforcement and the sample corpus for long-doc preflight.

sam: thanks. filing a short post with graphs and the failed pairs link in #eng-ml-postmortems. will keep the canary running at reduced split for a few hours to collect more samples.

jen: thumbs. small note: for customers on strict SLAs, we should exclude them from quant canaries by default. ops-bot can we add an opt-out label?

ops-bot: noted. policy update queued: "sla_exempt=true" label will exclude hosts from quant canaries when set.

sam: good call. thanks all.
